market_question: Will Trump and Putin meet next in another EU country?
reasoning: A Trump-Putin meeting during the Sep 2025–Jun 2026 window is plausible (around 50% chance) given Trump’s push for Ukraine talks. Conditional on a meeting, an EU venue is unlikely due to the ICC warrant and anti-Russia sentiment, but Hungary (EU member) remains a credible host, giving ~5% conditional probability, for a joint ~2.5% chance—well above the market’s 0.4%. This mispricing makes ‘Yes’ undervalued.
evidence_points: Trump has repeatedly stated he will meet Putin to negotiate Ukraine peace.
Hungary’s Orbán maintains friendly ties with both leaders and has signaled willingness to host Putin despite the ICC warrant.
Other EU countries have strongly opposed Putin’s travel and would face domestic backlash for hosting him.
The 9-month timeframe is long enough for at least one summit, with non-EU neutral locations (e.g. Saudi Arabia) being the default.
sources_consulted: Reuters reports on Trump-Putin meeting prospects (2025)
BBC coverage of Hungary’s stance towards Putin’s ICC warrant
General geopolitical analysis of EU-Russia relations post-2022
